Never, on any timescale that matters. The premise is a myth.

At room temperature glass is an amorphous solid, not a slow liquid. Estimates of its viscosity put the time for noticeable flow far beyond the age of the universe. Zanotto (1998) calculated relaxation times on the order of 10³² years for cathedral glass. Roman glassware and centuries-old telescope lenses show no measurable sag, which they would if glass flowed.

Old church panes are uneven because of how they were made. Crown glass was spun into a disc that came out thicker in some areas than others, and glaziers usually set the heavy edge at the bottom for stability. Some old panes were installed with the thick edge at the top or side, which wouldn't happen if gravity were the cause. Modern float glass is uniform from the start.

If your windows ever look warped, the cause is the frame, the seals, or a failed double-glazed unit, not the glass flowing.
